deutsche-bank-internship-programme-2027.about: Open to any degree discipline for penultimate-year students (graduating 2028 for the 2027 programme), with no more than 12 months of full-time work experience. In Germany you need at least three bachelor's semesters.
deutsche-bank-internship-programme-2027.eligibility: Penultimate-year student, at most 12 months of full-time experience, any discipline; right to work in the host country.
how_to_apply: Open the official programme page and check which offices and divisions are recruiting for your graduation year.
Prepare a CV in English (and a cover letter if requested) and upload your transcript.
Submit the online application; you may be limited in how many divisions or offices you can apply to.
Complete the online assessments or recorded video interview within the window given in the invitation email.
Attend the interviews or assessment day; strong interns can receive a full-time return offer.

deutsche-bank-spring-into-banking.about: Spring into Banking is for students in their first year of study. At the end of the week you gain early access to the interview process for the Summer Internship Programme.
deutsche-bank-spring-into-banking.eligibility: First-year students; right to work in the UK or Ireland; English.
how_to_apply: Open the programme page.
Apply with CV.
Complete assessment.
Attend the week.

dnb-central-bank-internships.about:
The DNB careers site lists three internships at the central bank in Amsterdam, each at master's level and 32-36 hours per week: Financial stability and financial markets; Data and Tech; and (Macro)economics and monetary economics.

The listing page does not state duration, pay, nationality rules or deadlines; open the individual vacancy for those (the vacancy pages could not be read when checked).
dnb-central-bank-internships.eligibility: Master's-level students. Nationality, language and work-permit rules are not stated on the listing page; check the vacancy text.
how_to_apply: Open werkenbijdnb.nl and the internship listings
Open the vacancy that fits your field
Apply as described in the vacancy
dnb-central-bank-internships.costs: Pay and duration are not stated on the listing page.

dpjw-german-polish-youth-exchange-projec.about:
The German-Polish Youth Office (offices in Potsdam and Warsaw) supports exchanges through organisations and schools that apply for funding: youth encounters, trilateral projects, '4x1' micro-projects, 'Wege zur Erinnerung' history projects, TRIYOU projects with Ukraine, vocational projects and MINT exchange experiments.

Students usually take part through their school, club or youth organisation, which files the funding application; the DPJW site provides a partner search and applications guidance. The public page does not state a single age range or deadline.
dpjw-german-polish-youth-exchange-projec.eligibility: Groups, schools and youth organisations in Germany and Poland (and partners in trilateral projects); the page does not state ages.
how_to_apply: Read the funding section and partner search on dpjw.org.
Ask your school or youth organisation to apply, or find an existing exchange.
Follow the application and accounting guidance.
dpjw-german-polish-youth-exchange-projec.costs: DPJW funds a share of project costs according to its published funding rates (see the 'Funding rates' page).

eba-young-talents-programme-2027.about:
The EBA's Young Talents programme covers high-school job shadowing (unpaid, on site), a students programme for post-secondary and higher-education students (unpaid), and a traineeship for university graduates with a monthly grant and teleworking options.

Job shadowing and student applications go by email with a CV and motivation letter; traineeships are only accepted through official vacancy notices.
eba-young-talents-programme-2027.eligibility: Job shadowing: high-school students aged 14-19. Students programme: post-secondary or higher-education students. Traineeship: university graduates. The page states no nationality requirement. Applications in English.
how_to_apply: Job shadowing: email CV and motivation letter to EBA-internships@eba.europa.eu with preferred units, dates and duration
Students programme: email CV and motivation letter to EBA-student-programme@eba.europa.eu
Traineeship: email a Europass CV, one-page motivation letter, eligibility grid and diplomas to EBA-Traineeship-Applications@eba.europa.eu in response to a published call
eba-young-talents-programme-2027.costs: Job shadowing and students programme unpaid (possible canteen support); traineeship paid with a monthly grant (amount not on the page).

ebrd-internships-london.about:
The EBRD does not run a single formal internship scheme but recruits interns on an ongoing basis to fill junior roles in banking, risk, economics, legal, IT and other departments. Contracts run from 6 to 12 months, mainly in London and some country offices.

Postings are searchable by department on the EBRD jobs site.
ebrd-internships-london.eligibility: Typically a national of an EBRD member country (stated in the vacancy); degree-level study in a relevant field, strong English, analytical and Excel skills. Some roles are reserved for specific nationalities (for example Japanese nationals).
how_to_apply: Search the early-career opportunities on the EBRD jobs site.
Open the vacancy and check nationality and study requirements.
Click Apply and submit CV and cover letter before the posting end date.
Complete the assessment if shortlisted.

eca-ai-traineeship-april-2027.about:
This ECA programme targets graduates (three-year diploma or more) or current doctoral students in AI, computer science, data science, IT or a related field. The linked call is for the April 2027 session.

Applicants email a Europass CV, a cover letter and a recommendation letter in English or French. The grant is EUR 2,500 per month.
eca-ai-traineeship-april-2027.eligibility: EU member state nationality. University diploma of three years or more, or enrolment in doctoral studies, in AI, computer science, data science, IT or similar. Very good knowledge of one official EU language and satisfactory knowledge of a second, plus English at least C1. No prior work for any EU institution, body or agency, including as a trainee.
how_to_apply: Prepare a Europass CV, a cover letter and a recommendation letter (English or French)
Email them to ECA-AI-Traineeship@eca.europa.eu by 30 November 2026 (midnight Luxembourg time)
eca-ai-traineeship-april-2027.costs: Monthly grant EUR 2,500 (only the difference is paid if you already receive another allowance).

eca-traineeships-2027.about:
The ECA offers standard traineeships of six months in Luxembourg in two yearly sessions (1 April to 30 September, 1 October to 31 March). The monthly grant is EUR 2,000.

A separate positive-action programme for trainees with a recognised disability (EUR 2,300 per month, two places a year) and a programme for auditors from candidate-country audit institutions also exist.
eca-traineeships-2027.eligibility: EU member state nationality. University diploma of three years or more. Very good knowledge of one official EU language and satisfactory knowledge of a second. No prior work for any EU institution, body or agency, including as a trainee.
how_to_apply: Open the ECA traineeships page
Click 'apply' next to the open session
Complete the online application form
Disability applicants email proof of disability to the address on the page
eca-traineeships-2027.costs: Monthly grant EUR 2,000 (Positive Action EUR 2,300). No fees stated.

ecb-traineeship-programme.about:
The ECB advertises traineeships by division (monetary policy, financial stability, markets, audit and more) on its talent portal, with PhD traineeships for doctoral students.

Postings state the grant and an accommodation allowance or free ECB residence in Frankfurt.
ecb-traineeship-programme.eligibility: Many postings are open to EU nationals; a bachelor's or higher in a relevant field; C1 English. Check each vacancy for nationality rules.
how_to_apply: Search ECB traineeship vacancies on talent.ecb.europa.eu.
Check nationality and degree rules.
Apply online before the vacancy end date.
Interview.

ecdc-traineeship-2028.about:
ECDC runs one annual traineeship call for graduates early in their careers. The 2027 programme starts between February and April 2027; interviews run to mid-December 2026, and a reserve list is valid until 31 December 2027.

This record is for the next yearly call; the current one is closed.
ecdc-traineeship-2028.eligibility: Citizens of an EU Member State, Norway, Iceland or Liechtenstein (a residence permit alone does not qualify). Full university degree by the application deadline. Very good English. No previous EU institution, agency or body traineeship or employment. Medical students who have not completed their degree are not eligible.
how_to_apply: Wait for the next yearly call on the ECDC traineeship page
Apply through ECDC's e-recruitment system
Reapplication in a later period is allowed if unsuccessful
ecdc-traineeship-2028.costs: Monthly grant (EUR 2,205.72 in 2026) plus travel allowance; trainees pay income tax and need health insurance valid in Sweden; no help finding housing.

eesc-traineeships-2027.about:
The EESC runs long-term traineeships twice a year for university graduates, and short-term paid placements of one to three months for students who need the traineeship to complete their studies. The long-term grant is EUR 1,538.88 a month.

Selection is anonymous and applicants must not contact EESC services to support their application.
eesc-traineeships-2027.eligibility: Long-term: university graduates (or a letter from the university confirming a completed three-year degree-level education). Short-term: students who need the traineeship for their studies. The page does not state nationality rules; these are in Decision No 166/23 A, linked on the page.
how_to_apply: Read Decision No 166/23 A on EESC traineeships
Complete the online form at candform.eesc.europa.eu
If pre-selected, upload diplomas and ID/passport when asked by email
If selected, provide a police record extract and medical certificate
eesc-traineeships-2027.costs: Monthly grant EUR 1,538.88 (long-term); travel and mobility allowance under Decision No 167/23 A.

ef-exchange-year-usa.about:
The EF Exchange Year site (efexchangeyear.org) shows how students from countries such as Italy, Spain and Germany live in U.S. host homes and study at a local high school. Students stay for a semester or school year; host families can also welcome a student for the first 2-3 months while a longer placement is arranged.

The public site is aimed mostly at host families and does not publish student fees or scholarships. Students apply through EF's local offices or partner agencies in their home country, so ask the nearest EF office for the programme price, the application deadlines and the visa (J-1) steps.
ef-exchange-year-usa.eligibility: International high-school students (typically 15-18 for J-1 school exchange). Exact age, English level and country availability are set by EF's local office; the public page does not list them.
how_to_apply: Visit efexchangeyear.org and contact EF (exchangeyear@ef.com) or the EF office in your country.
Ask about price, deadlines, English test and the J-1 visa steps.
Complete the application and host family matching.
ef-exchange-year-usa.costs: Fees are not published on the public page; host families are not paid. Ask the EF office for the programme price.

eib-traineeship-programme-2027.about:
The EIB offers traineeships of three to five months in its teams, mainly at its Luxembourg headquarters. There are two intakes a year, in March-April and September-October, announced about four months in advance on the EIB job portal.

Selection is for advertised positions only and includes digital and panel interviews. Trainees receive a flat-rate monthly allowance of EUR 1,500 and one reimbursed round trip.
eib-traineeship-programme-2027.eligibility: Nationals of an EU member state or an EU candidate country (page lists Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia, Turkiye, Ukraine). Final-year university student, or graduate with under one year of work experience since the last degree (traineeships under nine months do not count). Proficiency in English and/or French. Qatar citizens are not listed.
how_to_apply: Go to the EIB job portal
Filter 'Job category' by 'Traineeship & GRAD programmes'
Submit an online application for an advertised traineeship
Selection includes digital and panel interviews
eib-traineeship-programme-2027.costs: EUR 1,500 flat-rate monthly allowance; one round trip from the point of origin reimbursed; accommodation is the trainee's responsibility.

embl-undergraduate-internships.about:
EMBL welcomes undergraduates in biology, chemistry, physics, mathematics, medicine, informatics and engineering. Internships are normally part of a Diploma, Bachelor's or Master's thesis at another institution, though standalone internships are considered.

There is no central application: you browse the research units, pick groups that fit and email the Group Leader directly. Whether the placement is paid depends on the group, so ask early about funding (for example EMBO short-term fellowships or your home university's mobility grants).

EMBL also runs separate named schemes such as the Lautenschlager 'Talents teach talents' summer school for non-biology undergraduates.
embl-undergraduate-internships.eligibility: Undergraduate (and master's) students in natural sciences, medicine, informatics or engineering; typically doing a thesis or project at their home institution. No nationality restriction is stated. Internships are arranged individually with group leaders, so acceptance and any pay depend on the group.
how_to_apply: Browse the EMBL research units and shortlist groups
Email the Group Leader(s) with a CV, transcript and a short motivation
Agree dates, project and funding with the group
Arrange visa, insurance and housing
Questions: undergraduates@embl.de
embl-undergraduate-internships.costs: Not stated; some groups pay a stipend, others do not. Applicants should secure their own funding (e.g. EMBO fellowships, home-university grants) if the group cannot pay.

epfl-excellence-research-internship-2027.about:
The Excellence Research Internship Program (ERIP) lets high-achieving students from partner universities spend about three months in an EPFL laboratory. The timeline is flexible between February and August depending on the lab.

Partner universities: McGill, UBC, Toronto and Waterloo (Canada); NTU Singapore; Carnegie Mellon, Georgia Tech, Johns Hopkins, UC San Diego and Illinois Urbana-Champaign (US). Students are nominated by their home international office (McGill and Toronto students apply directly).

This is a nomination-based programme: students from other universities should email EPFL to check whether they can apply.
epfl-excellence-research-internship-2027.eligibility: Top-10% Bachelor's or Master's student who has completed at least the second year of a Bachelor's, enrolled at an EPFL partner university (McGill, UBC, Toronto, Waterloo, NTU Singapore, CMU, Georgia Tech, Johns Hopkins, UCSD, UIUC), and nominated by the home international exchange office (not required at McGill and Toronto). Students at other North American or Singapore institutions can email EPFL to ask. Not open to students at universities outside these partners, including in Georgia or Qatar, unless they are enrolled at one of them.
how_to_apply: Check your university is an EPFL partner and ask your international office about nomination
Prepare transcript, CV and motivation letter
Submit the online application by 30 November 2026
Ensure reference letters are uploaded by 6 December 2026
Wait for lab matching; start date agreed with the host lab
epfl-excellence-research-internship-2027.costs: No fee. EPFL pays an excellence scholarship for a maximum of three months (amount not stated on the official page). Travel and visa are the student's responsibility.

erasmus-plus-blended-short-term-mobility.about:
Short-term mobility lets higher education students and doctoral candidates spend 5 to 30 days abroad at a partner institution, always combined with a virtual component (only doctoral candidates may do a short stay without the virtual part). It is organised by your university and counts towards the 12-month limit per study cycle.

There is no central application form: contact your university's international office, which selects students and signs the grant agreement.
erasmus-plus-blended-short-term-mobility.eligibility: Students enrolled at an Erasmus+ participating higher education institution; doctoral candidates may go without the virtual part. Ask your university about nationality and partner-country rules.
how_to_apply: Ask your international office which short-term blended mobilities it offers.
Apply in its selection round.
Sign the grant agreement and complete the virtual component and stay.
erasmus-plus-blended-short-term-mobility.costs: Erasmus+ grant contributes to travel and daily living costs; the amount varies by destination and number of applicants.

erasmus-plus-student-credit-mobility-eur.about:
Erasmus+ exchange is organised by your own university: there is no central application form. You must be registered at a higher education institution that takes part in Erasmus+ and be enrolled in a programme leading to a recognised degree. Mobility can take place within Erasmus+ countries and to and from associated countries.

Long-term stays last 2-12 months; the maximum is 12 months per study cycle (24 for one-cycle courses such as medicine or architecture), possibly in several stays. Students sign a learning agreement before leaving and the home institution recognises the ECTS credits afterwards. The grant contributes to travel and living costs and varies with destination; host tuition, registration and exam fees are waived. Extra support exists for traineeships, students with fewer opportunities and students with disabilities.

Each university runs its own selection round, so ask the international office about its internal deadline.
erasmus-plus-student-credit-mobility-eur.eligibility: Students at short-cycle, bachelor, master or doctoral level registered at an Erasmus+ participating institution. Nationality rules are not set centrally: ask your university. Students from partner and associated countries can join via their university's bilateral agreements.
how_to_apply: Contact the international/Erasmus+ office of your university.
Apply in your university's internal selection round with the documents it asks for.
Sign the learning agreement with the host and sending institutions.
Sign the grant agreement and travel.
erasmus-plus-student-credit-mobility-eur.costs: Host tuition, registration and examination fees are waived (small insurance or student union fees may apply). The EU grant contributes to travel and living costs; the amount depends on destination.

esa-graduate-trainee-programme-2027.about:
The ESA Graduate Trainee programme places recent graduates in ESA's engineering, science, operations and support teams for up to a year. Trainees work on real missions and projects at an ESA establishment such as ESTEC (Noordwijk), ESRIN (Frascati), ESOC (Darmstadt) or ESAC (Madrid).

Candidates are final-year Master's students or recent graduates in engineering, science, IT or business-support fields. Applicants register a profile on the ESA careers portal with a CV and motivation letter and answer pre-screening questions on nationality and degree. Vacancies are published together in an annual call, usually in February.

It is one of the most direct routes into the European space sector.
esa-graduate-trainee-programme-2027.eligibility: Final-year Master's student or recent graduate in engineering, science, IT or business support. Applicants must be nationals of an ESA member state or cooperating state; nationality and degree are checked by pre-screening questions in the application form. Check the ESA page for the current list of cooperating states (it determines whether e.g. Georgian or Qatari citizens can apply). Good English required; French is an asset.
how_to_apply: Watch the ESA careers pages for the annual call (expected around February 2027)
Create a candidate profile on the ESA jobs portal with CV and motivation letter
Answer the nationality and degree pre-screening questions
Apply to the trainee vacancies that match your field
Attend remote interviews if shortlisted
esa-graduate-trainee-programme-2027.costs: Paid by ESA; no application fee. The traineeship allowance (set per vacancy) covers living costs.

etf-traineeship-turin-2027.about:
The ETF offers a full-time 12-month traineeship at its premises in Turin with a monthly allowance of EUR 1,300. Trainees from non-EU countries may get help from the ETF's relocation agency with residence permit applications.

Opportunities are announced in calls for applications on the ETF site.
etf-traineeship-turin-2027.eligibility: The page states no nationality requirement and notes that trainees from non-EU countries may receive help with residence permits. Educational and language criteria are in the individual call.
how_to_apply: Watch the ETF traineeship page and Application process page for open calls
Apply as described in the call
etf-traineeship-turin-2027.costs: Monthly allowance EUR 1,300; travel contribution if residence is more than 200 km from the ETF.

eurojust-traineeship-2027.about:
Eurojust takes trainees twice a year (October and March starts). Calls for interest are published on the Eurojust Recruitment Portal; email and speculative applications are not accepted, and interviews are online.

Trainees must hold health insurance valid in the Netherlands for the whole traineeship.
eurojust-traineeship-2027.eligibility: Nationals of EU Member States or EU candidate countries; nationals of third countries with a cooperation agreement or working arrangement with Eurojust may be accepted in exceptional cases, depending on budget. Recent university, master's or doctorate graduate (diploma by the closing date). B2 English certificate. No more than six weeks of prior in-service training or work in any EU institution, body or agency.
how_to_apply: Wait for the call (published twice a year)
Submit via the Eurojust Recruitment Portal
Interviews are online; only invited candidates are contacted
eurojust-traineeship-2027.costs: Monthly grant EUR 1,500 and contribution to travel costs at start and end; trainee pays Dutch-valid health insurance.

european-ombudsman-traineeship-2027.about:
The European Ombudsman advertises paid traineeships through yearly notices, normally published in February with a 1 September start. A positive-action programme for trainees with a recognised disability has run since 2023.

Applications must be in English. Trainees may be placed in Strasbourg or Brussels. The pay amount is not stated on the careers page.
european-ombudsman-traineeship-2027.eligibility: University or higher-education graduate status and a keen interest in the EU project. The careers page does not state nationality rules; full criteria are in the Ombudsman's Decision on traineeships linked from the page. Applications in English.
how_to_apply: Watch the careers page for the yearly traineeship notice (normally February)
Read the job notice and the Decision on traineeships
Apply in English through the online account linked on the page
european-ombudsman-traineeship-2027.costs: Paid; the amount is not stated on the careers page.

fao-internship-programme.about:
FAO, the UN agency on food, agriculture and fisheries, places interns from 3 to 11 months in Rome headquarters, regional and country offices. Individual interns receive a stipend of up to USD 700 per month depending on duty station; sponsored interns follow the stipend set by their sponsoring institution. Accommodation is not covered.

Individuals apply through the ongoing Call for Interest in FAO iRecruitment; universities and institutions can apply separately through the institutional collaborations call.
fao-internship-programme.eligibility: Aged 21 to 30 at the start; student in a degree programme or graduate within two years; nationals of FAO Member States (Georgia and Qatar are members); working knowledge of an FAO official language. No parent/sibling employed by FAO.
how_to_apply: Create a profile in FAO iRecruitment.
Apply to the ongoing Call for Interest vacancy.
Or have your university apply via the institutional collaborations call.
If matched, a unit contacts you.
fao-internship-programme.costs: Stipend up to USD 700/month; accommodation, travel and visa at intern's cost.

flex-global.about:
FLEX Global is the U.S. Department of State's merit-based high-school exchange, which brings together the Future Leaders Exchange (FLEX) and the Kennedy-Lugar Youth Exchange and Study (YES). It is run by American Councils for International Education with AFS, Amideast and iEARN.

Finalists spend a full school year with a screened volunteer host family, attend a U.S. high school, do community service and take part in leadership activities. Everything is paid for: flights, a monthly allowance, school, insurance and orientations.

Selection is free and merit-based: an English test, proctored essays and an interview. Recruitment runs separately in each participating country (Jordan, Morocco, Brazil, Tunisia, Armenia, Bahrain, Egypt, Georgia, India, Indonesia, Kazakhstan, Kenya, Kyrgyzstan, Moldova, Mongolia, Poland, Romania, Serbia, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Türkiye, Ukraine, Uzbekistan), so the dates and the birth-date window depend on where you apply from.
flex-global.eligibility: Citizens of a participating country who are enrolled in secondary school there, usually in grade 9, 10 or 11 (each country's round publishes the exact birth-date window). Good academic standing, previous English study, U.S. J-1 visa eligibility and an international passport. Students whose family has applied or plans to emigrate to the U.S. are not eligible.
how_to_apply: Find your country in the list of countries and deadlines on this page
Open your country's FLEX Global page to check the round dates and birth-date window
Register on ais.americancouncils.org/flexglobal and take the English test
Write the proctored essays and attend the interview if you advance
Submit the full application; finalists are announced in spring

fred-hutch-ship-2027.about:
SHIP is a competitive eight-week, 40-hours-a-week internship at the Fred Hutch campus in South Lake Union, Seattle: two weeks of lab technique and safety training, then six weeks in a faculty lab. Interns receive a financial award on successful completion (amount given at interview) and a free ORCA card.

Applicants must have completed 11th grade, be at least 16 by the start, and live in Greater Seattle; out-of-state and international students are not accepted. No housing or transport is arranged.

The application has four 200-word essays, two references, a transcript and a resume, and a Zoom interview. Notifications come by mid-May.
fred-hutch-ship-2027.eligibility: Rising high-school seniors (completed 11th grade), 16+, living in Greater Seattle; out-of-state and international students not accepted; available all eight weeks; Zoom interview required.
how_to_apply: Open the portal from 11 Jan 2027
Fill the four essays, resume and transcript
Send recommendation links to two referees
Submit by 8 Mar 2027, 11:59pm PT
Attend the Zoom interview
fred-hutch-ship-2027.costs: Financial award on completion (amount shared at interview); free ORCA card; no housing or parking provided.

gist-global-intern-program.about:
The Global Intern Program of the Gwangju Institute of Science and Technology places international students in GIST schools and departments for research experience. Applicants must be undergraduate seniors or master's students; non-qualifying applications are not considered.

The online application (2 to 27 February in 2026) requires an account, degree certificates, official English transcripts, a letter of recommendation, an English proficiency result and two preferred laboratories with a research plan. Each school or department selects its own interns.

The page we could read does not state duration, stipend or housing, so confirm these with GIST's Section of International Relations before applying.
gist-global-intern-program.eligibility: International undergraduate seniors or master's students. No nationality restriction stated. English proficiency certificate (or proof of English-medium instruction) required.
how_to_apply: Create an account with your email on the GIST application site
Complete the online form and choose two preferred laboratories
Upload degree certificates, official English transcripts, a recommendation letter, English test result and research plan
Wait for the departments' selection
gist-global-intern-program.costs: Funding, housing and fees are not stated on the page; confirm with GIST before applying.

goethe-institut-washington-internship.about:
The Goethe-Institut does not run one central internship programme: each local institute posts its own. The Washington institute offers placements of about three months in cultural, language and programming departments.

The allowance is voluntary, so plan to fund your stay. Check the page for current openings and requirements.
goethe-institut-washington-internship.eligibility: University students; German and English skills normally expected. Interns arrange their own US visa and work authorisation; check the current call.
how_to_apply: Open the Washington internship page
Check current calls and requirements
Send the application documents named there
goethe-institut-washington-internship.costs: No guaranteed stipend; interns pay for living and accommodation.

goldman-sachs-summer-analyst-emea-2027.about:
The Summer Analyst Programme is Goldman Sachs's main route for university students into its EMEA divisions. Interns work on live projects and are assessed for a return offer to the New Analyst Programme.

Goldman Sachs also publishes parallel programmes for the Americas and Asia-Pacific; see the regional pages.
goldman-sachs-summer-analyst-emea-2027.eligibility: Students due to graduate in 2028 (penultimate year); any degree subject. Candidates need the right to work in the office they apply to; check the page for sponsorship details. Fluent English.
how_to_apply: Open the official programme page and check which offices and divisions are recruiting for your graduation year.
Prepare a CV in English (and a cover letter if requested) and upload your transcript.
Submit the online application; you may be limited in how many divisions or offices you can apply to.
Complete the online assessments or recorded video interview within the window given in the invitation email.
Attend the interviews or assessment day; strong interns can receive a full-time return offer.

google-software-engineering-internship-s.about:
Google's Software Engineering Intern (BS) roles for Summer 2027 are published on the Google Careers site, in several countries and offices. Interns join a team, work on a real project and are paired with a host and mentor.

Recruiting is competitive and rolling in the autumn; strong data structures and algorithms skills are tested in interviews. Locations and exact eligibility (including work authorisation) differ per posting, so read the posting for your target office.
google-software-engineering-internship-s.eligibility: Students enrolled in a bachelor's programme (BS roles; MS and PhD roles are posted separately). Eligibility, location and work-authorisation rules are stated per posting; check the posting for your country. Strong English and CS fundamentals expected.
how_to_apply: Open the Software Engineering Intern (BS) Summer 2027 postings on Google Careers
Choose the office/country you are eligible to work in
Submit CV and transcript
Complete the interview rounds (data structures and algorithms)
google-software-engineering-internship-s.costs: Paid internship; pay and relocation vary by location and are given on the posting. Google does not charge any application fee.

halyk-start-it-internship-almaty.about:
Halyk Start is Halyk Bank's internship for talented IT students and graduates. Interns work on non-trivial challenges in Halyk ecosystem projects, with an official salary that grows with professionalism and a performance bonus.

Applicants should be in at least their third year of any IT discipline (or graduates), live in Almaty or be willing to move there. Duration and deadlines are not stated.

Apply through the form on the programme page: name, contact details, university and specialty, technical skills, optional CV (up to 5 MB).
halyk-start-it-internship-almaty.eligibility: Students from 3rd year in any IT discipline or graduates; based in Almaty or willing to relocate. Nationality rules and work-permit requirements are not stated on the page; the form is in Russian.
how_to_apply: Open the Halyk Start page
Fill in the on-page form (name, phone, email, university, specialty, skills)
Optionally attach a CV (up to 5 MB) and consent to data processing
halyk-start-it-internship-almaty.costs: Paid: official salary and performance bonus; amount not published.

human-rights-watch-internships.about:
Human Rights Watch posts internships per office and division on its job board, aimed at undergraduate and graduate students. Applicants normally send a CV, a letter of interest and a writing sample.

Pay varies by office. Several US listings are unpaid, while some European offices give an hourly allowance. Check each posting before applying.
human-rights-watch-internships.eligibility: Undergraduate and graduate students (some postings open to first- to third-year undergraduates). Work authorisation for the office country is the applicant's responsibility; check the posting.
how_to_apply: Browse current internship postings on the HRW careers portal
Prepare a CV, letter of interest and a writing sample
Apply online (email applications are not accepted)
human-rights-watch-internships.costs: Unpaid in many US offices; Paris allowance EUR 5.50 per hour attended; other offices vary.

iaea-internship-programme.about:
IAEA interns work in technical, legal, policy and administrative departments at Vienna headquarters or the Seibersdorf laboratories. Full-time interns receive a EUR 1,450 monthly stipend and medical insurance; travel and visa costs are the intern's. Placements run three months to a year.

A separate Marie Sklodowska-Curie Fellowship Programme funds women in nuclear fields with master's scholarships and internships (up to EUR 1,000/month).
iaea-internship-programme.eligibility: At least 20; three years of full-time university study completed; apply within one year of finishing a bachelor, master or doctorate; no previous IAEA internship. Nationals of IAEA Member States (Georgia and Qatar are members); English proficiency.
how_to_apply: Find internship vacancies on the IAEA careers page.
Submit the online application with CV and motivation.
Provide university proof.
Arrange travel, visa and housing after selection.
iaea-internship-programme.costs: EUR 1,450/month stipend plus medical insurance; travel and visa at intern's cost.

iaeste-technical-internships.about:
IAESTE places students with employers, labs and universities abroad for technical work experience, usually in engineering, IT and the sciences, with some management, marketing and language roles. Placements run from about eight weeks to a year.

You register on the IAESTE exchange platform, browse open internships and apply through your national or local IAESTE committee; if you are accepted by the employer you prepare the documents (cover letter, CV, module list, enrolment certificate, insurance). Some committees charge registration or placement fees, and internal selection rules differ by country.

Students from countries without an IAESTE committee follow a different process described on the IAESTE site.
iaeste-technical-internships.eligibility: Currently enrolled in a bachelor's, master's or PhD programme, or a graduate within one year of finishing, in a country with an IAESTE committee. Some committees ask for one completed year of study and set their own grade or language rules. Students from non-member countries follow a separate process. Check whether your country (e.g. Georgia or Qatar) has a national committee on the IAESTE site.
how_to_apply: Register on the IAESTE exchange platform
Contact your national or local IAESTE committee for their selection rules and deadline
Browse open internships and apply for those that fit
Prepare cover letter, CV, module list, enrolment certificate and insurance
Start once the host employer accepts you
iaeste-technical-internships.costs: Internships are normally paid by the host; the student pays travel, insurance and any committee registration/placement fee.

icc-internship-visiting-professional-pro.about:
The ICC hosts interns in Chambers, the Office of the Prosecutor, the Registry and other organs, working on international criminal law research, case analysis, outreach and administration. Interns are enrolled in a graduate programme, in the final year of a first degree, or hold a degree, with less than three years of relevant full-time experience; people with more experience may be Visiting Professionals.

Placements are generally unfunded, but the Trust Fund for the Development of Interns and Visiting Professionals finances some placements for citizens of eligible States Parties to the Rome Statute (Georgia is a State Party). Anyone of any nationality can apply for unfunded places.
icc-internship-visiting-professional-pro.eligibility: Enrolled in a graduate programme, in the last year of a first degree, or holding a degree from an accredited university, with under three years of relevant experience. Strong English or French. Open to all nationalities for unfunded places; funded places only for citizens of eligible States Parties (Georgia yes; Qatar is not a State Party). No parent or sibling working at the ICC.
how_to_apply: Check ICC internship vacancy announcements on the careers page.
Submit the online application with CV and motivation letter.
If funded places are offered, indicate eligibility under the Trust Fund.
Arrange visa and accommodation if selected.
icc-internship-visiting-professional-pro.costs: Generally unfunded; some Trust Fund placements. Travel, living and insurance costs are the intern's unless funded.

icj-judicial-fellowship-programme.about:
The Judicial Fellowship Programme places about 15 outstanding law graduates, each assigned to a judge, for research and drafting on pending cases. Only universities can nominate candidates (the Court takes no individual applications), and candidates are generally under 31 at the start.

The programme runs from early September to June. A Trust Fund set up in 2021 supports fellows from developing countries whose universities cannot sponsor them. There is also a separate ICJ Internships page for unpaid Registry placements posted as vacancies.
icj-judicial-fellowship-programme.eligibility: Law graduates nominated by their university (universities must complete a pre-screening form and name a focal point); generally no older than 31. Strong English or French. Open to any nationality if your university participates; ask your law faculty to nominate you.
how_to_apply: Ask your university law faculty to nominate you.
The university completes the pre-screening questionnaire and focal-point registration.
Submit application materials through the focal point before the deadline.
Court decides by around April for a September start.
icj-judicial-fellowship-programme.costs: Unsalaried; fellows are expected to be funded by their university or sponsor, with Trust Fund support for eligible developing-country candidates.

ilo-internship-programme.about:
The ILO places graduate students and recent graduates in its Geneva headquarters and field offices, working on labour standards, employment policy, social protection, statistics, legal and communications work.

Interns receive a stipend (Geneva postings cite CHF 2,450 per month; field-office rates are lower), reduced by any funding from a university or foundation. Travel is at the intern's own cost, though candidates from under-represented countries may get airfare help. The Internship Roster opens twice a year, normally April and October; specific vacancies are advertised too.

Special internships for persons with disabilities also exist.
ilo-internship-programme.eligibility: In the final year of a graduate (master or equivalent) degree, or completed one within the past year. Working knowledge of English, French or Spanish. No close relatives on ILO staff; former ILO interns cannot reapply. Open to nationals of ILO Member States, including Georgia and Qatar.
how_to_apply: Go to jobs.ilo.org and open the Internship page.
Register in the internship roster when it is open (April/October).
Complete your profile, CV and motivation.
Respond if a unit shortlists you.
ilo-internship-programme.costs: Stipend in Geneva about CHF 2,450/month; travel, visa and housing at the intern's own expense (airfare support possible for under-represented countries). No fee.

imf-fund-internship-program-2027.about:
The Fund Internship Program places graduate students in IMF departments to work on an individual research project under an IMF supervisor. PhD students are placed as economist interns; master's students can apply to specialised tracks.

It is one of the best-known entry points into international economic policy work and a common route to later IMF recruitment programmes such as the Economist Program.
imf-fund-internship-program-2027.eligibility: Graduate students only (PhD for economist internships, master's for specialised internships), under 32 at entry, enrolled in a graduate programme; the internship must be done in Washington, DC for its full duration. Strong spoken and written English. Previous participants cannot reapply. Check the page for nationality and visa conditions.
how_to_apply: Read the eligibility rules on the Fund Internship Program page.
Create a profile on the IMF careers portal and upload your CV, transcripts and a research statement.
Submit the application for the department track that matches your field.
Complete any assessment and interviews if shortlisted.
imf-fund-internship-program-2027.costs: Paid internship; travel and visa arrangements are described on the programme page.

iom-internship-programme.about:
IOM, the UN migration agency, offers internships in Geneva headquarters, regional hubs and country offices, in migration policy, data (Displacement Tracking Matrix), border management, legal affairs, communications and ICT. Several DTM internships are explicitly labelled paid.

Interns generally receive a stipend as a partial contribution to accommodation and living costs, unless a university or sponsor already pays them. Candidates of any nationality may apply; selected interns must provide a fit-to-work medical certificate and vaccination records.
iom-internship-programme.eligibility: Enrolled in a degree programme or graduated within about 12 months; usually at least 20 years old (some sources note an upper age of 36); open to all nationalities, including Georgia and Qatar. Fluent English, often another language. Medical fitness certificate required.
how_to_apply: Find internship vacancies on IOM's e-Recruitment portal.
Apply with CV and motivation letter.
Provide enrolment/graduation proof.
Supply medical certificate and vaccination records if selected.
iom-internship-programme.costs: Small monthly stipend per IOM policy; travel, visa and housing costs at the intern's own expense.

iter-internship-programme.about:
ITER is the international fusion energy project under construction in Cadarache. Interns work with staff on technical, scientific or administrative topics for up to six months, extendable to a year.

Applicants must be enrolled in a bachelor's, master's or PhD programme at an accredited institution in an ITER Member country, have strong grades and fluent English; recent graduates are not eligible. You need a passport of China, the EU, India, Japan, South Korea, Russia or the USA (the UK is not currently accepted).

Choose up to five topics on the SuccessFactors portal and upload CV, cover letter with preferred dates and proof of nationality. The page does not mention a stipend; interns are not staff.
iter-internship-programme.eligibility: Enrolled bachelor's, master's or PhD students (not recent graduates) at an accredited institution in an ITER Member country; passport of China, EU, India, Japan, South Korea, Russia or USA; fluent English. Georgian citizens qualify only if they hold an EU/other Member passport; Qatar is not a Member.
how_to_apply: Open the ITER internships page and pick up to five topics
Register on the SuccessFactors portal and complete the questionnaire
Upload CV, cover letter with dates and proof of nationality
Submit within a window (16 Nov-13 Dec 2026 or 1-28 Mar 2027)
iter-internship-programme.costs: No stipend is mentioned on the page; interns are not ITER staff.

itu-internship-programme.about: ITU lists internships as part of its HR Partnerships Programme, with vacancies in an 'Internship' category on its jobs portal. The programme page sets the eligibility rules; the extract available at check time did not state duration, stipend or work location, so confirm these in each vacancy notice.
itu-internship-programme.eligibility: Under 30 years old (exceptions can be made for PhD candidates); enrolled in an undergraduate, graduate or postgraduate programme, or a graduate within six months of the internship; citizen of an ITU Member State; proof of enrolment or graduation certificate and CV required.
how_to_apply: Browse the 'Internship' category on the ITU jobs portal
Read the How to apply page
Apply to a vacancy with CV and proof of enrolment or graduation
itu-internship-programme.costs: Pay, if any, is not stated on the programme page; check the vacancy notice.

j1-au-pair-usa.about:
Au pairs must be 18 to 26, proficient in spoken English, a secondary school graduate or equivalent, pass an in-person English interview and a background investigation (school verification, three non-family references, criminal check, personality profile) and a medical check.

The placement is 12 months and can be extended by 6, 9 or 12 months. Au pairs get room and board, pay under the US Fair Labor Standards Act, at least 32 hours of childcare training, at least two weeks' paid vacation and one full weekend off each month, and must complete at least six hours of academic credit at a US accredited post-secondary institution (host family contributes up to $500). Hours are limited to 10 per day and 45 per week. The EduCare option has up to 30 hours of weekly childcare for 75% of the weekly rate and requires 12 hours of credit.
j1-au-pair-usa.eligibility: Age 18-26, secondary school graduate or equivalent, spoken English, interview, background checks, medical check.
how_to_apply: Find a licensed Au Pair sponsor on the j1visa.state.gov sponsor search.
Apply, pass the English interview and background checks.
Match with a host family and complete childcare training.
Obtain the DS-2019 and J-1 visa.
j1-au-pair-usa.costs: Room and board with the host family, pay for childcare, up to $500 from host family toward required coursework; sponsor programme fees apply (check with sponsor).

j1-camp-counselor-usa.about:
Participants must be at least 18, be a foreign post-secondary student, youth worker, teacher or person with specialised skills, and speak English well enough to supervise American youth. Counsellors receive pay and benefits comparable to American counterparts, and may do some non-counselling camp duties but cannot work as administrators, cooks or custodial staff.

The State Department page does not give the programme length; summer camp seasons typically run a few weeks to a couple of months, so confirm with the sponsor. Apply through a designated J-1 sponsor.
j1-camp-counselor-usa.eligibility: At least 18; foreign post-secondary student, youth worker, teacher or someone with specialised skills; good English.
how_to_apply: Search for a Camp Counselor sponsor on j1visa.state.gov.
Apply through the sponsor and complete interview and background checks.
Get your DS-2019 and attend the J-1 visa interview.
j1-camp-counselor-usa.costs: Not stated on the official page; sponsors may charge programme fees. Counsellors are paid by the camp.

j1-college-university-student-exchange.about:
To qualify, funding must come from a government, an international organisation or another substantial source other than personal or family funds, or the exchange must be under an agreement between governments or educational institutions. Participants must be admitted to an accredited US post-secondary institution and be enrolled full-time.

Non-degree programmes last a maximum of 24 months including academic training; degree programmes run to completion. Student internships that meet degree objectives at home also qualify. The host institution or sponsor verifies academic credentials before issuing the DS-2019.
j1-college-university-student-exchange.eligibility: Admitted to an accredited US post-secondary institution; full-time enrolment; funding from a government, international organisation or substantial non-family source, or exchange under an inter-government or inter-institutional agreement.
how_to_apply: Get admitted to the US institution (usually via an exchange agreement with your home university).
Request the DS-2019 from the host institution or sponsor.
Attend the J-1 visa interview.
j1-college-university-student-exchange.costs: Not stated on the official page; depends on host university, scholarship and sponsor.

j1-secondary-school-student-exchange.about:
Under J-1, a foreign student aged at least 15 and not more than 18 years and six months at programme start (or having completed no more than 11 years of primary and secondary school) can attend a US school as an exchange visitor. The student must apply through a State Department-designated sponsor; the sponsor handles host family placement and school enrolment.

A student who has already done a secondary school academic year or semester exchange in the US, or attended a US school in F-1 or J-1 status, is not eligible. Programme length (academic year or semester) is set by the sponsor.
j1-secondary-school-student-exchange.eligibility: Aged 15 to 18 years and 6 months on the programme start date (or no more than 11 years of schooling); no previous US school exchange or F-1/J-1 school attendance.
how_to_apply: Open the Find a Program Sponsor search on j1visa.state.gov.
Choose a sponsor that runs the Secondary School Student category in your country.
Apply to the sponsor; it issues the DS-2019 and guides the visa interview.
j1-secondary-school-student-exchange.costs: Fees and scholarships are set by each sponsor (some sponsors, such as government-funded programmes, are free).

j1-summer-work-travel-usa.about:
Participants must be full-time post-secondary students at an accredited classroom-based institution outside the US, have completed at least one semester (or equivalent) and be proficient in English. The maximum stay is four months and participants must return home before their school term starts; they may take part more than once.

Applicants from Visa Waiver Program countries do not need a pre-arranged job, while non-visa-waiver applicants must be pre-placed in a job before entry. Employers must pay at least the higher of state or federal minimum wage. Participants apply through a designated sponsor found in the State Department sponsor search.
j1-summer-work-travel-usa.eligibility: Full-time post-secondary student outside the US, at least one semester completed, proficient English; must return home before the next term. Country rules vary: non-visa-waiver applicants need a pre-arranged job. The page does not state a minimum age.
how_to_apply: Check the State Department sponsor search for an SWT sponsor in your country.
Apply to the sponsor and complete the English test and interview.
Secure (or get placed in) a job as the sponsor requires.
Follow the sponsor's guidance for the J-1 visa interview.
j1-summer-work-travel-usa.costs: The State Department page does not state costs. Sponsors charge programme fees; check the sponsor's price before applying.

jane-street-software-engineering-interns.about:
Internships typically last 10 to 12 weeks between May and September, with off-cycle options at each office. Jane Street says it looks for curious people from any background with a passion for technology and creative problem solving; interns have come from over 24 countries.

The company also runs first- and second-year programmes (Bridge, FTTP, FOCUS, WiSE) as short insight days rather than internships.
jane-street-software-engineering-interns.eligibility: No degree or class-year requirement is listed; check the posting for the office. Visa/work-permit conditions are per office.
how_to_apply: Open the internships page on janestreet.com
Pick the role and office
Submit application and take the technical interviews
jane-street-software-engineering-interns.costs: Paid; amount not stated on the page.

jax-animal-care-pre-apprenticeship.about:
This hands-on pre-apprenticeship at The Jackson Laboratory pays USD 19.25 per hour plus an $8 daily lunch subsidy over nine summer weeks, at the Ellsworth and Bar Harbor campuses.

You must be enrolled in a Maine high school, in 11th grade, at least 16 by the end of the school year, with a strong work ethic and interest in hands-on teamwork. No residency rules beyond Maine enrolment are listed. Apply through the 'How to Apply' page.
jax-animal-care-pre-apprenticeship.eligibility: Enrolled in a Maine high school, in 11th grade, 16+ by the end of the school year. Not open to students outside Maine.
how_to_apply: Open the JAX 'How to Apply' page
Complete the application by 27 March
Attend any interview
jax-animal-care-pre-apprenticeship.costs: Paid USD 19.25 per hour plus USD 8 per day lunch subsidy.

jax-summer-student-program-2027.about:
The JAX Summer Student Program places undergraduates in a research lab at The Jackson Laboratory for 10 weeks. 2027 dates: Bar Harbor, ME 5 June-13 August (residential) and Farmington, CT 31 May-8 August (not residential).

Admission is competitive and high school seniors are no longer accepted. Students must attend the whole programme and may not hold another job, internship or summer class. The page links to separate eligibility FAQs for citizenship and international applicants, which should be read before applying.

The stipend is USD 7,500 plus room and board, and round-trip travel is provided. Virtual open houses are held 8 Dec, 14 Dec and 5 Jan.
jax-summer-student-program-2027.eligibility: Undergraduate students (high school seniors no longer accepted); must attend the full programme. Citizenship and international eligibility are on JAX's separate eligibility FAQ, not on the admission page.
how_to_apply: Register with NSF-ETAP
Complete the NSF-ETAP application for JAX SSP
Follow the link to the JAX SSP application
Submit both applications by 25 Jan 2027, 5pm ET
jax-summer-student-program-2027.costs: Paid USD 7,500; room, board and round-trip travel provided.

jenesys-jice-youth-exchange-japan.about:
JICE's youth exchange division (jice.org/exchange) organises inbound programmes such as JENESYS and the KAKEHASHI Project for the Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Participants travel as delegations; the sample schedule on the site covers nine days, and programmes run for about ten days in different parts of Japan, with school exchanges among peers.

The public page does not list ages, eligible countries or the application process: individual participants are normally selected by the sending organisation or schools in the partner region, not by direct application to JICE. Watch the JICE site for open calls (for example the Japan-Africa Youth Program notice of August 2026) and ask your school or ministry whether your country's delegation is recruiting.
jenesys-jice-youth-exchange-japan.eligibility: Delegation-based: eligibility depends on the sending organisation and partner region (ages and countries are not stated on the public page). Watch for calls on the JICE site.
how_to_apply: Open the JICE Youth Exchange page and read 'Program in Japan' and the FAQ.
Ask your school, ministry or partner organisation if your country is part of the current delegation.
Contact JICE (+81-3-6838-2730) for open calls.
jenesys-jice-youth-exchange-japan.costs: Typically covered by the Japanese government for selected delegates; confirm with the organiser for each call.

jpmorgan-investment-banking-summer-analy.about:
Interns join an investment banking team, work on live client projects and are trained in valuation and modelling. High performers may receive an offer of continued employment at the end of the nine weeks.

Locations differ by year; the application portal only displays locations where the programme is open.
jpmorgan-investment-banking-summer-analy.eligibility: University students in their penultimate year; the page asks for analytical, quantitative and interpretative skills. Right to work in the chosen location is typically needed; check the portal.
how_to_apply: Open the official programme page and check which offices and divisions are recruiting for your graduation year.
Prepare a CV in English (and a cover letter if requested) and upload your transcript.
Submit the online application; you may be limited in how many divisions or offices you can apply to.
Complete the online assessments or recorded video interview within the window given in the invitation email.
Attend the interviews or assessment day; strong interns can receive a full-time return offer.

jpmorgan-private-bank-summer-internship-.about:
The Private Bank's Asia-Pacific early-career pages list a 2027 Global Private Bank Advisor Program summer internship in Hong Kong and an Investment Solutions Program internship in Singapore.

If you graduate in 2027 you are directed to the full-time programmes instead.
jpmorgan-private-bank-summer-internship-.eligibility: Students not graduating in 2027 (those graduating in 2027 apply to full-time roles); right to work in Hong Kong or Singapore; English.
how_to_apply: Open the official programme page and check which offices and divisions are recruiting for your graduation year.
Prepare a CV in English (and a cover letter if requested) and upload your transcript.
Submit the online application; you may be limited in how many divisions or offices you can apply to.
Complete the online assessments or recorded video interview within the window given in the invitation email.
Attend the interviews or assessment day; strong interns can receive a full-time return offer.

jsps-summer-program-japan.about:
The JSPS Summer Program, run with SOKENDAI, gives young researchers an introduction to Japanese science and culture: an orientation, Japanese language lessons and about two months of research under a host researcher at a Japanese university or institute.

It is open to citizens of the United States, United Kingdom, France, Germany, Canada and Sweden, applying through national partner bodies (such as CNRS, DAAD, the Canadian embassy/NRC and STINT); citizens of other countries with equivalent status may apply if a nominating authority approves.

You need a confirmed host researcher in Japan and must be enrolled in a graduate programme or have received a doctorate on or after 2 April 2021.
jsps-summer-program-japan.eligibility: Citizen of the US, UK, France, Germany, Canada or Sweden (others with equivalent status only if approved by a nominating authority in those countries); enrolled in a graduate programme or PhD obtained on or after 2 April 2021; prior acceptance by a host researcher in Japan; aspiration to a research career; not a previous JSPS Summer Program fellow; not Japanese nationals or residents. Citizens of Georgia and Qatar are not named on the page.
how_to_apply: Identify and contact a host researcher in Japan and secure acceptance
Find your national nominating authority (e.g. DAAD, CNRS, NRC/Canada, STINT)
Submit the application through that authority
Await selection, then arrange visa and travel
Join the orientation and start research
jsps-summer-program-japan.costs: No fee. JSPS covers airfare, a JPY 534,000 allowance and insurance (tentative amounts).

kaist-visiting-student-researcher-progra.about:
The Visiting Student Researcher programme lets students enrolled (or on leave) at a university outside South Korea carry out research in a KAIST lab for one month to one year. Undergraduates are not excluded; recommended criteria are one year of full-time undergraduate study, GPA 3.0/4.3 or higher and TOEFL iBT 80 or equivalent.

You must first arrange a topic and period with a KAIST professor and obtain approval, then apply through the KAIST IO System at one of four quarterly deadlines. The page does not describe any stipend; a research-allowance confirmation is requested only 'if applicable', and housing is not provided by default.

This is a self-arranged research visit rather than a paid internship, so budget for the USD 350 non-refundable registration fee, living costs and the Korean visa.
kaist-visiting-student-researcher-progra.eligibility: Currently enrolled (or on leave) at a university outside South Korea; undergraduates allowed. Recommended: 1 year of full-time study, GPA 3.0/4.3, TOEFL iBT 80 or equivalent. Written approval from a KAIST professor required. No nationality restriction stated.
how_to_apply: Agree a research topic and dates with a KAIST professor and get approval
Prepare the VSR application, home-supervisor confirmation letter, host-lab confirmation form, enrolment certificate and passport copy
Submit via the KAIST IO System by the quarterly deadline
Pay the USD 350 fee after approval, then apply for the Korean visa
kaist-visiting-student-researcher-progra.costs: USD 350 non-refundable registration fee. No stipend described on the page; accommodation not provided by default; visa and living costs are the student's.

kek-sokendai-summer-student-program.about:
The SOKENDAI KEK Summer Student Program places students in research groups at the High Energy Accelerator Research Organization (KEK) in Tsukuba and at J-PARC in Tokai, working on particle and nuclear physics, accelerator science, materials and life science. Participants join a host group for up to eight weeks between mid-June and mid-August (theory groups: up to four weeks), with joint sessions in mid-to-late July.

It targets students in the latter half of an undergraduate course or the early part of a master's programme (not PhD students) from Japan or abroad. Knowledge of dynamics, electromagnetism and quantum mechanics is desirable but not required, depending on the host group.

International participants receive airfare, KEK/J-PARC dormitory fees, domestic travel from Narita/Haneda and JPY 1,500 per day; visas and medical insurance are not covered. A recommendation letter is mandatory.
kek-sokendai-summer-student-program.eligibility: Students in the latter half of an undergraduate course or early in a master's programme as of 1 March of the year (not PhD), international or Japanese. No nationality restriction stated; Georgian and Qatari citizens are not excluded by the page. Recommendation letter required.
how_to_apply: Register online to obtain an ID number and arrange a recommendation letter
Submit CV, transcript and the application form through the web form (files under 5 MB, ID number in file names)
Your recommender submits the letter separately with your applicant code
Wait for results (2026 cycle: notified by end of April)
kek-sokendai-summer-student-program.costs: No fee stated. International participants: airfare, dormitory, domestic transfer and JPY 1,500/day covered; visa and insurance are the participant's responsibility.

lfx-mentorship-linux-foundation.about:
LFX Mentorship is the Linux Foundation's open-source mentorship platform. Mentees work on scoped tasks in a real project under a mentor, fully online.

Not every programme is funded; where a stipend is offered its size varies by programme and by country of residence and is paid in milestones. Prior open-source experience is not required, and school enrolment is needed only for some programmes. You can have up to three applications at a time and may complete only one LFX mentorship in your career.
lfx-mentorship-linux-foundation.eligibility: Aged 18 or over, able to commit consistent hours for the full term, and not previously completed an LFX mentorship. No nationality restriction is stated on the page (stipend amounts depend on country of residence); school enrolment is required only for some programmes.
how_to_apply: Create an LFX profile on the mentorship site
Browse programmes that are open for the current term
Apply to up to three projects, following each project's instructions
Complete any pre-selection task set by the mentors
lfx-mentorship-linux-foundation.costs: Free to apply. Some projects pay a stipend; others are unpaid.

loreal-internships.about:
L'Oréal calls internships the number-one route to a job at the company. Postings are filtered by contract type on its careers site and you can create alerts for 'Internship'.

You may apply to a maximum of three positions in any 30-day period. Duration, eligibility and pay are not stated on the home page and depend on the country and the posting.

This is the internship route only; it is separate from the Brandstorm competition.
loreal-internships.eligibility: Students enrolled in higher education; conditions per posting (country, language, internship agreement with your university).
how_to_apply: Open the L'Oréal internships page
View all opportunities and filter by contract type 'Internship'
Create an alert and apply (max 3 applications per 30 days)
loreal-internships.costs: Paid per local law; amounts per posting.

mckinsey-summer-business-analyst-intern.about:
McKinsey's Business Analyst Intern programme (8-10 weeks) puts students on client teams solving real problems. Campus pages exist for many universities; students from other schools apply via the general page.

There is also a 10-12 month Business Analyst Intern programme in Mexico City or Monterrey.
mckinsey-summer-business-analyst-intern.eligibility: Undergraduate students, typically a year before the final year; deadlines and office choices vary by school. Right to work in the chosen office; English.
how_to_apply: Check the campus page for your university or the general page.
Submit CV, transcript and application.
Complete the problem-solving test.
Case interviews.

microsoft-discovery-program-2027.about:
Discovery is a four-week internship for students about to start their first year of university, based in Redmond, Washington or Atlanta, Georgia. It introduces participants to Microsoft's teams and tech careers before they begin their degree.

It is the closest Microsoft option for current high-school seniors. Pay, housing and visa rules are not stated on the overview page, so confirm them on the posting.
microsoft-discovery-program-2027.eligibility: Students who are about to begin their first year of university (typically current high-school seniors). Work-authorisation and nationality conditions are on the posting; US-based programme.
how_to_apply: Open the Discovery Program listing on Microsoft Careers
Check dates and your work authorisation
Submit application with CV
Complete assessment/interview if invited
microsoft-discovery-program-2027.costs: Microsoft internships are paid employment, but the page does not state the amount; confirm on the posting.

microsoft-explore-program-2027.about:
Explore is Microsoft's summer internship for first- and/or second-year college students, focused on software development. It is designed for students who have little or no prior internship experience and combines hands-on engineering work with mentoring and community events.

Microsoft asks first-year and second-year applicants not to apply to both versions when both are posted. Check the Microsoft careers student page for current postings and rules on work authorisation.
microsoft-explore-program-2027.eligibility: First- or second-year university students in a bachelor's programme. US postings normally require work authorisation for the US; check the posting for details.
how_to_apply: Open the Explore Program page on Microsoft Careers
Pick the first- or second-year posting that matches your year
Upload CV/resume and submit
Complete the online assessment/interviews if invited
microsoft-explore-program-2027.costs: Paid internship; compensation is stated on the posting. No application fee.

mit-lincoln-lab-llrise-2027.about:
LLRISE is a project-based radar workshop run by MIT Lincoln Laboratory; the 2026 edition ran 12-25 July with students living in MIT dormitories and working at MIT and Lincoln Lab in Lexington. Tuition is free and transport to Lincoln Lab is provided; students pay travel to MIT.

Applicants must be US citizens (permanent residents are not eligible) completing junior year. This is a workshop rather than a paid internship, listed here because it is Lincoln Lab's main high-school pathway; no 2027 dates have been published yet.
mit-lincoln-lab-llrise-2027.eligibility: US citizens only (not permanent residents), completing 11th grade, strong in science, math and engineering. Not open to international students.
how_to_apply: Watch the LLRISE page for the 2027 application
Apply online (2026 deadline was mid-March)
Arrange recommendations
mit-lincoln-lab-llrise-2027.costs: Free tuition; students pay their own travel to MIT.

mitacs-globalink-research-internship-202.about:
Globalink Research Internships place undergraduates from eligible partner countries in a research project at a Canadian university for 12 weeks between May and October. A Canadian professor supervises the project and an on-campus student mentor supports the intern.

The 2027 cycle covered Austria, Brazil, Chile, China, Colombia, Finland, France, Germany, Hong Kong, India, Ireland, Jordan, Mexico, Pakistan, Peru, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand, Tunisia, Ukraine, the UK and the US. Georgia and Qatar were not on that list, so check each year's list.

Applicants rank several projects across different Canadian provinces; the funding package depends on the country and host institution.
mitacs-globalink-research-internship-202.eligibility: Full-time undergraduate (or combined undergraduate/master's) at an institution in an eligible partner country, at least 18 years old, with two years of study completed and 1-3 semesters left in fall 2027; country-specific grade minimums; fluent English and/or French; never previously awarded a Globalink internship. Applicants must apply to several projects across at least three provinces. Citizens of countries not on the partner list (the 2027 list did not include Georgia or Qatar) cannot apply.
how_to_apply: Check that your country and university are on the current Globalink partner list
Subscribe to Mitacs updates and wait for the call to open (about six weeks)
Prepare transcript, CV, statement and reference
Browse Canadian projects and rank at least three across three provinces
Submit through the Mitacs application portal and await matching
mitacs-globalink-research-internship-202.costs: No fee. Mitacs funds partial round-trip airfare, airport transfer, housing/food/incidentals (amount depends on country and host), and emergency health insurance.
